# Candor UI design system

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/build-design.mjs from src/styles/candor.css and src/styles/candor-theme.css. Change the CSS (colours: scripts/theme.mjs), then run npm run agents. -->

The tokens Candor UI's components are drawn with, and how to build the screens around them. Every value here is read from the shipped CSS. The look is a dense, quiet application: small type on near-white or near-black grounds, hairline borders rather than shadows, one brand hue for the one primary action, and status in words beside any colour. Light, dark and high-contrast themes share the same roles, and every text and ground pairing is checked for contrast (44 pairings in each of 3 themes) before the CSS is written.

`candor.css` holds the tokens, keyframes and utilities; it imports `candor-theme.css`, which holds the colours. Import `candor.css` after Tailwind (the `candor-ui init` command does this); override anything in a file imported after it.

## Colour roles

Colour roles use shadcn's variable names where shadcn has one (`--primary`, `--background`, `--muted-foreground`), so shadcn components already in an app pick them up, and Candor's own roles take the `--cd-` prefix, so an app's own tokens can't collide with them (`--cd-sunken`, `--cd-chrome`, `--cd-success-weak`). Each is also a Tailwind colour: `bg-sunken`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border-strong`. Values are OKLCH, so a role keeps its lightness when its hue changes. Before 4.0 Candor's own roles had no prefix (`--sunken`, `--warning`) and the chart series were `--series-1` to `--series-6`; nothing reads those names now, so a brand file that sets them changes nothing. [Upgrading to 4.0](https://candor.themethodic.com/upgrading-to-4#tokens-cd-prefix) lists each rename, `npx candor-ui migrate tokens` makes them, and `npx candor-ui theme check` reports an old name as an error.

What things sit on. Choose by depth and job, not by taste: the page, a surface on it, a well set into it, a floating layer above it.

### Status

4 status hues (`destructive`, `warning`, `success`, `attention`), each in the same parts: `--cd-<hue>` the solid (a dot, a bar, a solid button; `--destructive` keeps shadcn's name), `--cd-<hue>-weak` a tinted ground, `--cd-<hue>-text` text on that ground or on card, and `--cd-on-<hue>` text on the solid where the kit uses the hue as a solid behind text (destructive and success). Never colour alone: the status word sits beside the dot.

## Type

| Token | Value | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--cd-font` | "Inter Variable", system-ui, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif | Everything. Inter when the `font-inter` item is installed, else the system's sans-serif. |
| `--cd-font-display` | "Inter Variable", system-ui, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif | Headings (`h1` to `h4`), set at optical size 32 and weight `--cd-weight-heading`. |
| `--cd-font-mono` | ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace | Code, queries, logs, keys. |

The scale is a dense app scale: `--cd-text-sm` is the body default and `--cd-text-md` the comfortable one. Each step is also Tailwind's `text-<step>` with the line height below (`--cd-text-md` is `text-base`).

| Token | Size | Line height | For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--cd-text-2xs` | 0.6875rem | 1rem | Fine print: a keyboard key, a count in a badge. |
| `--cd-text-xs` | 0.75rem | 1rem | Metadata: timestamps, status words, captions, table headers. |
| `--cd-text-sm` | 0.8125rem | 1.25rem | Body text in the app: lists, tables, forms, buttons. The `body` default. |
| `--cd-text-md` | 0.875rem | 1.375rem | Comfortable body: descriptions, dialogs, the base for conversation text. |
| `--cd-text-lg` | 1rem | 1.5rem | A section title or a lead sentence. |
| `--cd-text-xl` | 1.25rem | 1.75rem | A page title. |
| `--cd-text-2xl` | 1.5rem | 1.2 | A large figure or a page's main heading. |
| `--cd-text-3xl` | 1.75rem | 1.15 | A headline figure (a stat card's total), a report's title. |
| `--cd-text-4xl` | 2rem | 1.1 | A report's title on a wide screen. |
| `--cd-text-5xl` | 2.5rem | 1.05 | The largest step, for your own display text; no component uses it. |
| `--cd-text-prose` | var(--cd-text-md) | 1.375rem | Conversation text: messages and the composer. |

Body text is tracked at `-0.011em` (`--cd-tracking-body`); headings weigh 620 (`--cd-weight-heading`).

| `--cd-radius-xs` | 4px | Tiny tags, inline marks, a close button's focus ring. |

shadcn's `--radius` is `var(--cd-radius-lg)`. Each radius is Tailwind's `rounded-<name>` (`rounded-xl`, `rounded-button`, `rounded-tile`).

## Shadows and elevation

Hairline borders separate things at rest; shadows are for what floats. The shadow colour is `--cd-shadow`: `oklch(0.2 0.02 265 / 0.07)` in light, `oklch(0 0 0 / 0.35)` in dark.

| Token | Value | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--cd-elev-1` | 0 1px 2px var(--cd-shadow) | Resting: a card that needs a hint of lift. Tailwind `shadow-xs` and `shadow-sm`. |
| `--cd-elev-2` | 0 1px 2px var(--cd-shadow), 0 2px 8px var(--cd-shadow) | Raised: a `Surface` with `tone="raised"`, a dragged item. `shadow-raised`. |
| `--cd-elev-3` | 0 12px 40px -12px oklch(0.2 0.02 265 / 0.16), 0 1px 2px var(--cd-shadow) | Floating: popovers, menus, a `Surface` with `tone="floating"`. `shadow-float`. |
| `--cd-elev-4` | 0 2px 4px var(--cd-shadow), 0 16px 40px oklch(0.2 0.02 265 / 0.14) | Overlay: the heaviest, for full-screen layers of your own; no component uses it. `shadow-overlay`. |

## Motion

| Token | Value | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--cd-ease` | cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) | The standard easing for anything that appears or moves. Tailwind `ease-standard`. |
| `--cd-ease-inout` | cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) | For things that move and come back: a sheet or drawer sliding open, a toggle. `ease-inout`; most components use `ease-standard`. |
| `--cd-ease-spring` | linear(0, 0.4 15%, 0.7 30%, 1 50%, 0.95 65%, 1.02 80%, 1 100%) | A small overshoot for things that arrive, in your own motion. `ease-spring`. |

| Token | Value | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--cd-dur-quick` | 120ms | Something leaving, or a colour change. Tailwind `duration-(--cd-dur-quick)`. |
| `--cd-dur-base` | 200ms | Something arriving or opening: a collapse, a pop, a nudge. `duration-(--cd-dur-base)`. |
| `--cd-dur-slow` | 360ms | A mark being drawn or a rail filling after a status settled. `duration-(--cd-dur-slow)`. |

Motion reports a change that happened, never one that is predicted or decorative (the ninth honesty rule). Every animation belongs to one of fourteen families, one for each kind of change: `reveal` (content opening or closing to its measured size), `arrive` (something new after the first draw), `pop` (a chip or small mark added or removed), `mark` (a tick or cross drawn when a result settles), `fill` (a bar or ring moving between measured values), `value` (a number or word changing in place), `move` (a thing changing place), `overlay` (a dialog, sheet, popover or menu opening or closing), `press` (a press registered), `tint` (hover, focus, selected), `refuse` (a locked control pressed), `attention` (something new waits on the person), `live` (work being heard from) and `clock` (real time passing: a hold, a deadline). Each component moment (copy-field's tick, a dialog opening) belongs to one. The manifest `motion.json` lists every item's moments with their family, defaults and the sentence that says when each plays; it is served at `/r/v/<version>/motion-manifest.json` beside the registry, and each item's docs page has a Motion section built from it.

A family has a level (0 off, 1 subtle, 2 expressive), a duration, an easing, a size where it has one, and a closed set of variants: named ways of drawing the same change, of which a brand picks one and cannot add another. A brand file sets `--cd-motion-<family>` (the level), `-dur`, `-ease`, the family's amplitude and `-variant` for a family everywhere, or `--cd-motion-<item>-<moment>-*` for one moment of one component; `--cd-motion-speed` (0.5–1.5) scales every duration but the clock's and the attention ring's, which stays under five seconds. A brand changes how a change looks, never when it plays: the trigger stays in the component, so a brand cannot make a tick appear before the result or a bar fill ahead of the work.

Who decides, from the strongest: `data-motion="none"` on `<html>` or any container (nothing moves, whatever else is set), then the person's operating system (`prefers-reduced-motion`) or `data-motion="calm"` as the same choice made in the app (the calm level), then `data-motion="subtle" | "expressive"`, then the brand file, then Candor's defaults. No attribute is the brand's levels (subtle unless it says otherwise); `subtle` caps every family at 1; `expressive` raises the families the brand didn't set. The `clock` family is the exception to turning things off: a hold's progress or an undo window's time left is the information itself, so a brand can restyle it but not remove it. A mark that was already final when the page drew does not animate. Components build a moment's chain with `motion(item, moment, family)` from `lib/candor/motion.ts` and add the family utility (`cd-pop`, `cd-overlay`…) only at the honest moment.

| Family | Reports | Duration (range) | Easing (allowed) | Amplitude (expressive) | Variants (default first; fixed: one drawing, nothing to set) | Calm |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reveal` | Content opened or closed to its measured size; a chevron turns. | 200 ms (150–300) | standard (standard, inout) | — | `cd-size`, `cd-fade` | Snaps to its measured size. |
| `arrive` | Something new, added after the first draw. | 240 ms (150–300) | standard (standard, spring) | `-distance` 8px | `cd-rise`, `cd-fade`, `cd-pop` | Fades in, up to 150 ms. |
| `pop` | Added, removed, or a small mark appearing. | 200 ms (100–300); out 120 ms | standard (standard, spring) | `-scale` 0.85 | `cd-scale`, `cd-fade` | Fades, up to 150 ms. |
| `mark` | A tick or cross drawn when a result settles. | 360 ms (200–500) | standard (standard) | — | `cd-draw`, `cd-pop`, `cd-drop` | The finished mark fades in, up to 150 ms. |
| `fill` | A bar or ring moving between measured values. | 360 ms (200–600) | standard (standard, inout) | — | (fixed) | Snaps to the new value; its colour may fade. |
| `value` | A number or word changed in place. | 120 ms (80–200) | standard (standard) | `-distance` 2px | `cd-fade`, `cd-slide` | Crossfades, up to 150 ms. |
| `move` | A thing changed place: a reorder, a tab indicator, a toast restacking, a scroll. | 200 ms (150–300) | standard (standard, spring) | — | (fixed) | Jumps to its new place. |
| `overlay` | A dialog, sheet, popover, menu or tooltip opened or closed. | 150 ms (100–500); out 150 ms | standard (standard, inout, spring) | `-scale` 0.95 | `cd-scale`, `cd-slide`, `cd-fade` | Fades, up to 150 ms. |
| `press` | A press registered. | 150 ms (80–200) | standard (standard) | `-scale` 0.96 | (fixed) | Doesn't scale; the colour still answers. |
| `tint` | Hover, focus, selected, a drop target: a colour or opacity change. | 150 ms (0–200) | standard (standard, inout) | — | (fixed) | Colour and opacity only, up to 150 ms. |
| `refuse` | A locked control was pressed: the reason is shown, and under expressive it shakes. | 360 ms (200–500) | standard (standard) | `-distance` 3px | (fixed) | No shake; the reason's colour still changes. |
| `attention` | Something new waits on the person: a ring that grows and fades. | 900 ms (600–1600) | standard (standard) | `-count` 1 | (fixed) | One ring that fades without growing, up to 150 ms. |
| `live` | Work that is being heard from: a dot's pulse, a caret, a spinner, a shimmer, a skeleton. | 1600 ms (1000–3000) | standard (standard, inout, linear) | — | (fixed) | Still, with its word. |
| `clock` | Real time passing: a hold, a deadline, a replay. Painted from the clock. | From the clock | linear (linear) | — | (fixed) | Steps instead of gliding; never off. |

Easings are written as CSS: standard `var(--cd-ease)`, inout `var(--cd-ease-inout)`, spring `var(--cd-ease-spring)`, linear `linear`. Spring overshoots, so only families that move things in space accept it. A variant is written as its keyframe's name (`--cd-motion-mark-variant: cd-pop`).

The 2.2 `animate-<name>` utilities, the unprefixed keyframes they ran, and the 2.2 tokens for the pop scale and the shake were removed in 3.0 ([Upgrading to 3.0](https://candor.themethodic.com/upgrading-to-3) lists each with its replacement and the `npx candor-ui migrate motion-aliases` codemod); use the family utilities above. `shimmer-text` animates text that is still arriving (`StreamingText`, `ShimmerLabel`) and keeps the `shimmer` keyframes.

## Reduced motion

Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (or `data-motion="calm"`) the kit moves to its calm level. Only opacity and colour change over time, each in 150 ms or less. Nothing loops: `live` indicators go still and keep their word, `attention` is one ring that fades, `reveal` snaps open or shut, `clock` steps rather than glides, and the rest become a fade or a colour change; each family's calm form is in the table above. `data-motion="none"` turns the remaining fades off as well, for people who want no movement without the OS setting. Anything the families do not cover, such as your own animations or a third-party widget, runs in 0.001ms, once, and scrolling is instant. Nothing in a Candor screen depends on motion to be understood.

## For your own motion

Take the duration, easing and size from the family that fits the change, never a raw number of milliseconds: a `duration-200`, an `animate-in` or a `transition-all` in your own component skips the brand's settings and the person's own level (`subtle`, `expressive`). The calm level and `data-motion="none"` still catch it, only less precisely: a raw transition keeps its duration, where a family's is capped at 150 ms. Start the motion from the moment the change is true (the write resolved, the step finished, the item arrived while the page was open), not from the press or the first draw. `npx candor-ui lint` warns about the raw forms in a file that uses Candor components.

## Sound

Sound is a second, quieter way to say that something needs a person, and it is never the only way. Five events can have one, each tied to a change the interface already shows: a cue the person can see always comes with it.

| Event | Raised when | The visible cue that always comes with it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `needs-you` | A new approval, question or choice waits on this person. | The prompt or its row, the count in the page title, a notification. |
| `finished` | A run this person started has finished. | The result, a toast, the title count. |
| `failed` | A run failed, or a guardrail stopped it. | The error toast, which stays, with the way to recover. |
| `reply` | Another person (not an agent) replied in a thread this person is in. | The message and the unread count. |
| `silent` | A run this person started has not been heard from for longer than the app's stale time. | The words "No update since…" on the run. |

A brand file names the sound for an event with `--cd-sound-<event>`, a path in the app's own files (`--cd-sound-needs-you: "/sounds/needs-you.mp3"`), and sets how loud with `--cd-sound-volume` for all of them or `--cd-sound-<event>-volume` for one. `--cd-sound-<event>-ogg` names an Ogg alternative for browsers that play it; the MP3 is required. A brand file chooses which sound plays, not whether sound is on and not when.

The rules sound keeps:

- **Off until the person turns it on.** Nothing in the theme or the kit enables it. The app offers the choice (off, when away, always) and the person makes it; the click that turns it on also plays the chosen sound once, so they hear what they chose.
- **Raised from data, never from a mount.** A prompt appearing on screen is not news, since the page may have just loaded. A sound plays only for something that was not there when the component first drew, such as an approval that has just arrived.
- **Always with a visible cue.** Every event above has one. A sound is never the only signal, and nothing depends on hearing it.
- **Coalesced.** Ten approvals at once play one sound, and the same event plays at most once every three seconds.
- **Short and still.** At most 1.5 seconds, no loops, no speech.
- **Hosted by the client.** The files live in the app, at the paths the brand file names. Candor's site does not serve sound to apps in production.

Nothing is fetched until a sound plays: a page with sound off, or on with no event raised, requests no audio file. Components don't play sounds themselves. The app's attention hook does, from the events it offers and the person's setting.

## Layout

| Token | Value | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--cd-thread-width` | 48rem | The message column's width; also the longest comfortable measure for reading. |
| `--cd-sidebar-width` | 16rem | The app sidebar's width. |

## Density

`data-density="compact" | "spacious"` on `<html>` or any container changes the scale: compact tightens it for dense apps, spacious loosens it for reading. It reaches the type and layout, and the size of controls and rows. What changes in type and layout:

| Token | Default | Compact | Spacious |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--cd-text-prose` | var(--cd-text-md) | 0.875rem | 1rem |
| `--cd-text-md` | 0.875rem | 0.8125rem | 0.9375rem |
| `--cd-thread-width` | 48rem | 44rem | 52rem |
| `--cd-sidebar-width` | 16rem | 14rem | 18rem |

The size of controls and rows. Heights run on one ladder (`2xs`, `xs`, `sm`, none, `lg`) and a button is one step under a field: Button's default is `sm`, Input and Select's is the bare `--cd-control-h`. Components read the tokens in the form `h-(--cd-control-h-sm)` and `px-(--cd-control-px)`, so a brand file that sets a token reaches every control. Write that form in your own classes, not the named utilities (`h-control-sm`, `py-item-y`): `cn()` merges by what a class sets, and it recognises `h-(--cd-control-h-sm)` as a height, so a consumer's `h-10` still wins. It does not recognise the named utilities, and both classes would apply. No compact value is under 24px, the smallest target WCAG 2.2 allows without spacing around it.

| Token | Default | Compact | Spacious |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--cd-control-h-2xs` | 1.5rem | 1.5rem | 1.75rem |
| `--cd-control-h-xs` | 1.75rem | 1.625rem | 2rem |
| `--cd-control-h-sm` | 2rem | 1.75rem | 2.25rem |
| `--cd-control-h` | 2.25rem | 2rem | 2.5rem |
| `--cd-control-h-lg` | 2.5rem | 2.25rem | 2.75rem |
| `--cd-control-px-xs` | 0.5rem | 0.375rem | 0.625rem |
| `--cd-control-px-sm` | 0.625rem | 0.5rem | 0.75rem |
| `--cd-control-px` | 0.75rem | 0.625rem | 0.875rem |
| `--cd-control-px-md` | 0.875rem | 0.75rem | 1rem |
| `--cd-control-px-lg` | 1.25rem | 1rem | 1.5rem |
| `--cd-control-py` | 0.5rem | 0.375rem | 0.625rem |
| `--cd-control-gap` | 0.5rem | 0.375rem | 0.625rem |
| `--cd-area-min-h` | 4rem | 3.5rem | 4.5rem |
| `--cd-item-px` | 0.5rem | 0.5rem | 0.625rem |
| `--cd-item-py` | 0.375rem | 0.25rem | 0.5rem |
| `--cd-row-h` | 2.5rem | 2rem | 3rem |
| `--cd-row-px` | 1rem | 0.75rem | 1.25rem |
| `--cd-row-py` | 0.5rem | 0.25rem | 0.75rem |
| `--cd-cell-px` | 0.5rem | 0.375rem | 0.75rem |

## Themes

`data-theme` on `<html>` takes `dark` or `hc`; light is the `:root` default, so `data-theme="light"` means light whatever the system says. With no `data-theme` at all, the system's dark setting applies. `dark` and `hc` also work on an inner element (a dark panel in a light page). Each theme sets `color-scheme` (light: light, dark: dark, hc: light), so form controls and scrollbars follow. Tailwind's `dark:` variant follows `&:where([data-theme="dark"], [data-theme="dark"] *)`.

`data-syntax="highlight" | "off"` turns syntax colouring of code on or off, for the whole app or one `Payload`. Only text roles that pass contrast on the sunken well are used for it.

## Naming, and making it your own

`--cd-*` is Candor's own namespace: 56 tokens for fonts, the type scale, tracking, radius, shadows, easings, durations, motion presets, widths, and the sizes of controls and rows. Colours use the shadcn names above. Tailwind sees all of them through `@theme inline`, so utilities such as `bg-sunken`, `text-prose`, `rounded-button`, `shadow-float` and `ease-standard` resolve to the tokens, and an override reaches every component.

The quickest way is the free theme builder at https://candor.themethodic.com/theme-builder: it takes the brand's colours, sets type, shape, motion and sound, checks every pairing in every theme, and downloads `candor-brand.css` (the overrides, imported straight after `candor.css`) and `candor-theme.json` (the same values as design tokens, with each check's ratio). It runs in the browser and the theme is never sent anywhere; if you give it a font's address and press to load it, your browser fetches the font from that host, which sees the request, and an exported file with a font `@import` does the same in your app. Check the result with `npx candor-ui theme check` from the project root (it reads the CSS file named in components.json and the files that file imports). Writing the overrides by hand works the same way:

To re-token for a brand, override after the import, by role, in every theme you support:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "../styles/candor.css"; /* the path candor-ui init wrote */
@import "../styles/candor-brand.css"; /* the same folder */

/* Your brand, after Candor's defaults. Keep each role's job; change its value. */
:root {
  --primary: <your brand colour>;
  --cd-primary-hover: <a step darker>;
  --ring: var(--primary);
  --cd-font: "Your Sans", system-ui, sans-serif;
  --cd-radius-button: var(--cd-radius-md);
}
[data-theme="dark"] {
  --primary: <your brand colour, lighter, for dark grounds>;
  --cd-primary-hover: <a step lighter>;
}
```

- Change a role, not a use: every component reads the role, so one override is consistent everywhere.
- Keep the status pairs together: a new `--cd-success` needs a `--cd-success-weak` it sits on and a `--cd-success-text` that passes on it. Keep the 4 status hues distinguishable from each other and from the primary.
- Check contrast after you change a colour. Candor checks its own pairings before writing the CSS; it can't check yours.
- Point `--cd-font` at your typeface rather than restyling components; keep `--cd-font-mono` monospaced.
- Change density with `data-density` before changing sizes.
- Your product's words go through `LocaleProvider`, its strings and its nouns, not through forks of the components.

## Screens around Candor components

**Surfaces.** Build on `Surface` rather than hand-rolled cards. Its tones, from the page up: `plain` (`bg-card border`), `muted` (`bg-muted`), `subtle` (`bg-sunken border`), `raised` (`bg-card border shadow-raised`), `floating` (`bg-popover border shadow-float`), `accent` (`bg-accent-weak text-foreground`). Its paddings: `sm` `p-3`, `md` `p-4`, `lg` `p-6`. The page is `background`; a card is `card` with a hairline border; wells are `sunken`; only popovers, menus and dialogs cast a shadow. The frame (sidebar, header) is `chrome`.

**Rhythm.** Use Tailwind's spacing scale and the type scale's line heights; don't invent sizes. Keep reading text inside `--cd-thread-width`. Group with space before you group with lines, and lines before boxes. One primary action per view, in `primary`; the rest are outline or ghost buttons.

**Status.** A status is a word, with a colour beside it: `StatusDot` and the status strings carry both. `muted-foreground` for metadata, `faint-foreground` for the quietest marks.

**Writing.** Plain and measured. Say what happened, for whom, and what to do next; no superlatives, no exclamation marks, no claims the data doesn't support. Sentence case for everything, including buttons. Name the agent from your own data. Say "estimate" when it is one, "not measured" when nothing was. Candor's own strings are British English; every one of them is replaceable through `LocaleProvider`, so match your product's spelling there.

## Do and don't

From the honesty rules every Candor component keeps (https://candor.themethodic.com/principles):

**Model output is text, never markup.**

- Do: Adapters read model text as a small safe subset of markdown: paragraphs, lists, code, bold and italic. Links become plain text with the address beside them. Nothing a model writes is ever HTML.
- Don't: Render model text with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or a markdown library, or turn a URL the model wrote into a link.

**Unknown stays unknown.**

- Do: Fields the service didn't report are left empty or say “not measured”. Costs an SDK estimates are labelled as estimates. A run receipt with no measured cost says so instead of showing $0.00. A run nothing has been heard from lately says when it was last heard, not that it's running.
- Don't: Show a placeholder figure (a cost of $0.00, a duration of 0s, a count of 0) where nothing was measured, or an estimate without the word estimate beside it.

**A control that can't be used says why.**

- Do: Locked controls carry a reason, shown on hover and focus and read by screen readers: who can do it, what's missing, or what has to happen first.
- Don't: Use `disabled` on a control a person might expect to use; it hides the reason and the control from keyboard and screen-reader users.

**Nothing is pre-selected in a decision.**

- Do: Approve and reject, allow and deny start with neither chosen. Destructive choices never sit under a one-key shortcut, and the agent's own permission prompts can open on Deny.
- Don't: Pre-select Approve, mark a default choice as checked, or put a destructive answer under Enter.

**Approve the exact change.**

- Do: Approval requests carry a hash of the change; a decision is tied to that hash, and a change that drifted since is rejected by the system. The blocks refuse self-approval and can require two people for production.
- Don't: Apply a change the person didn't see, or keep an approval alive after the change moved.

**Reasoning is believed, not verified.**

- Do: Reasoning is shown as the model's own account and marked as unchecked. Evidence is shown as evidence: sources, test results, the diff.
- Don't: Present the model's reasoning as fact, or style it like evidence.

**The agent is always named, by the app.**

- Do: Every agent message names its agent from the app's data, never from model output. System lines are the app's own strings.
- Don't: Take the agent's name, or any system line, from model output.

**Say what can and can't be undone.**

- Do: Destructive actions say what they remove and whether it can be brought back, and the riskiest ones ask the person to type a name to confirm.
- Don't: Confirm a destructive action with only OK and Cancel, or say Restored, Undone or Deleted without saying what wasn't.

**Motion follows the outcome.**

- Do: Motion reports a change that happened and never predicts or decorates one: a success mark is drawn after the result settles, a rail fills only to the step that finished, and a state that was already final when the page drew does not animate. Every animation belongs to one of fourteen families (reveal, arrive, pop, mark, fill, value, move, overlay, press, tint, refuse, attention, live and clock), one for each kind of change. A brand can pick a family's variant, duration and easing, or turn it off, but never the moment it plays, because that stays in the component. When the OS asks for reduced motion, or the app offers the same choice, a calm level applies: only opacity and colour change, briefly, and nothing loops; an app's “none” turns even that off, and both outrank the brand.
- Don't: Show a tick before the result arrives, animate progress nobody measured, keep an animation looping when the OS asks for reduced motion, or let a brand change when something moves.
